knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8,

## The question and the raw export

Sequencing pipelines often export a table with ASVs in rows and samples in
columns, alongside a taxonomic assignment for each sequence variant. This
example reshapes that output for DietView, checks the read totals and retains
unresolved assignments. It compares pooled read proportions with mean relative
read abundance (RRA), then produces a figure, a sample matrix and an optional
dashboard.

The read counts in this example are simulated to illustrate the workflow.
They cannot support biological conclusions. The
[Salish Sea harbour seal case](case-study-dna-seals.html) uses published data.

```{r data}
library(DietView)
asv <- data.frame(
  asv = paste0("ASV", 1:8),
  taxonomy = c(
    "k__Animalia;p__Chordata;c__Actinopteri;o__Gadiformes;f__Gadidae;g__Gadus;s__morhua",
    "k__Animalia;p__Chordata;c__Actinopteri;o__Gadiformes;f__Gadidae;g__Gadus;s__morhua",
    "k__Animalia;p__Chordata;c__Actinopteri;o__Clupeiformes;f__Clupeidae;g__Clupea;s__harengus",
    "k__Animalia;p__Chordata;c__Actinopteri;o__Pleuronectiformes;f__;g__;s__",
    "k__Animalia;p__Arthropoda;c__Malacostraca;o__Euphausiacea;f__Euphausiidae;g__;s__",
    "k__Animalia;p__Mollusca;c__Cephalopoda;o__Myopsida;f__Loliginidae;g__Loligo;s__Loligo sp.",
    "k__Animalia;p__Chordata;c__Actinopteri;o__Gadiformes;f__Gadidae;g__;s__",
    "Unassigned"
  ),
  S1 = c(120, 80, 0, 0, 20, 0, 5, 2),
  S2 = c(0, 0, 520, 0, 25, 5, 0, 8),
  S3 = c(75, 30, 0, 22, 0, 0, 10, 1),
  S4 = c(0, 0, 90, 40, 60, 0, 0, 5),
  S5 = c(0, 0, 0, 30, 0, 20, 0, 2),
  S6 = c(400, 0, 150, 0, 0, 0, 12, 3)
)
meta <- data.frame(
  sample = paste0("S", 1:6),
  predator = rep("Illustrative marine predator", 6),
  season = c("winter", "winter", "winter", "summer", "summer", "summer"),
  site = c("A", "A", "B", "A", "B", "B")
)
head(asv[, 1:4])
meta
```

**Unit:** one sample (`S1`–`S6`). **Quantity:** DNA read count.
**Taxonomic source:** illustrative lineage labels, not verified WoRMS
assignments. **Important prerequisite for real data:** quality-control reads,
negative controls, remove non-target/host sequences, check contamination and
assignment thresholds *before* the workflow below. DietView does not perform
sequence denoising, primer filtering or taxonomic assignment.

## Audit counts and sampling metadata

```{r audit}
reads <- as.matrix(asv[setdiff(names(asv), c("asv", "taxonomy"))])
stopifnot(!anyNA(reads), all(reads >= 0), all(reads == round(reads)))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(meta$sample), identical(colnames(reads), meta$sample))
colSums(reads)
sum(reads)
```

Read depths differ substantially. A pooled-read percentage gives a deep
library more influence than a shallow one, whereas mean RRA gives each
positive sample equal weight.

## Convert ASVs into taxon–sample records

ASV1 and ASV2 have the **same reported taxonomic assignment**. Here we
aggregate their read counts **within sample** for a taxon-level summary,
so that the taxon–sample record share is not inflated by multiple ASVs
assigned to one named category. This does **not** imply that the original
ASVs are biologically identical or interchangeable. Preserve the original
ASV-level table for sequence-level questions and reproducibility.

```{r long}
long <- dv_from_wide(asv, taxa_in = "rows",
                     id_cols = c("asv", "taxonomy"),
                     sample_col = "sample", value_col = "reads",
                     meta = meta, collapse_by = "taxonomy")
head(long)
stopifnot(sum(long$reads) == sum(reads))
```

The lineage parser handles rank prefixes, blank ranks, `sp.` and the
`Unassigned` record. Missing taxonomic ranks become genuine `NA` values;
unassigned DNA remains in the denominator rather than silently disappearing.

```{r parse}
long <- dv_parse_lineage(long, col = "taxonomy")
head(long[, c("sample", "reads", "prey_name", "phylum",
                "family", "species")], 10)
```

For real sequences, audit whether an ASV or several ASVs should count as one
*taxon detection*. The decision depends on the reporting question and on the
confidence of the reference classification. An unassigned record is a DNA
observation but not a named prey species.

## Declare the input contract and normalize within samples

```{r prep}
spec_rra <- dv_spec(
  predator = "predator", stomach = "sample", prey_name = "prey_name",
  weight = "reads", weight_type = "rra", unit_label = "sample",
  covariates = c("season", "site")
)
prep <- dv_prepare(long, spec_rra, taxonomy = "columns", verbose = FALSE)
prep
```

`dv_prepare()` keeps the original `reads` column and adds a sample-normalized
column (`prep$spec$weight`). A sample's contributions should add to one, even
when some reads cannot be named to species.

```{r normalization}
rra_col <- prep$spec$weight
rra_totals <- tapply(prep$data[[rra_col]], prep$data$sample, sum)
round(rra_totals, 8)
stopifnot(all(abs(rra_totals - 1) < 1e-8))
```

### Pooled reads versus mean RRA

Use **two distinct specifications**: `"reads"` keeps pooled read counts;
`"rra"` standardizes each sample before pooling. `pct_w` is the percentage
of the quantity declared in the specification, not a measure of prey mass.

```{r currencies}
spec_reads <- dv_spec(
  predator = "predator", stomach = "sample", prey_name = "prey_name",
  weight = "reads", weight_type = "reads", unit_label = "sample",
  covariates = c("season", "site")
)
prep_reads <- dv_prepare(long, spec_reads, taxonomy = "columns",
                         verbose = FALSE)
pooled <- dv_rank_table(dv_tree(prep_reads), "Phylum")
mean_rra <- dv_rank_table(dv_tree(prep), "Phylum")
comparison <- merge(pooled[, c("label", "pct_w")],
                    mean_rra[, c("label", "pct_w")], by = "label",
                    suffixes = c("_pooled_reads", "_mean_rra"))
comparison
```

These two percentages can differ because sequencing depth differs between
samples; *neither* is a percentage of ingested biomass. Always state which was
reported, and never mix them without a documented rationale.

## Occurrence, rank uncertainty and visualization

```{r statistics}
tree <- dv_tree(prep)
dv_rank_table(tree, "Family")
dv_fo_table(prep, rank = "family")
dv_resolution(prep)
```

`pct_occ` counts distinct taxon–sample rows after collapsing repeated ASVs.
`pct_fo` is the proportion of positive sample IDs with a taxon detection; it
is not a probability of feeding and need not sum to 100 across taxa. `pct_w`
is mean RRA. The explicit unidentified node matters especially for the
`Unassigned` reads and higher-rank matches.

```{r figure}
dv_sunburst(tree, mode = "weight", title = "Illustrative DNA diet",
            subtitle = "Mean within-sample RRA; simulated ASV counts")
```

```{r by-season}
res <- dv_resolution(prep, by = "season")
res[, c("season", "finest_rank", "n_records", "p_weight")]
```

## Export a sample-by-taxon matrix

```{r matrix}
m <- dv_matrix(prep, rank = "family", currency = "weight")
round(m, 3)
stopifnot(nrow(m) == nrow(meta))
utils::write.csv(m, file.path(tempdir(), "asv_example_family_rra.csv"))
```

A zero means no **retained** read assignment for a family in that sample,
not biological proof of absence. A read-positive sample defines a
within-sample RRA denominator; failed or fully filtered assays need a
separate sample inventory and should not be silently counted as negatives.
Preserve the ASV table, controls, filtering script, reference taxonomy
database and version, and the detection pipeline.

```{r dashboard, eval=FALSE}
dv_build_html(prep,
  output = file.path(getwd(), "asv_demo_dashboard.html"),
  strata = "season", bands = c("occurrence", "weight"),
  title = "ASV tutorial: read-based diet (simulated)")
```

## Reporting checklist and limitations

A complete report gives read-depth distributions, negative and positive
controls, thresholds, sample exclusions, marker/primer targets, DNA extraction
batch, taxonomy reference and version, unresolved fraction, sample-level
replication, currency and denominator, and uncertainty from the sampling
design. Do not read RRA as biomass, %FO as ingestion probability, or pooled
read share as an unbiased estimate of the prey's importance.

For a worked analysis of real scats, continue to
[harbour seal DNA in the Salish Sea](case-study-dna-seals.html). For samples
with **no prey sequence retained**, keep a separate sample inventory;
otherwise a long table cannot reveal their existence.

**Further reading:** Deagle et al. (2019), *Molecular Ecology* 28:391–406,
<https://doi.org/10.1111/mec.14734>.
